Subject: POC: org + network MAP and POC environment checklist

Hi Raj / Heather —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our discussion, I put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on getting your POC environment live so you can evaluate throughput and latency on a representative workload. Attached is a draft MAP (MAP_DataHealth_v0.3.xlsx) and a minimal allowlist stub for ops teams.

High-level asks we need to complete before kick-off (suggested 2-week timeline):
- Redwood: provision evaluation org (org ID), temporary API keys with scoped access, and a POC model bundle pinned for the test.
- DataHealth: provide public egress IP ranges to add to our allowlist, preferred VPC peering window (maintenance-friendly), and an internal security contact for SOC/Q verification.
- Procurement/legal: confirm whether a PO or signed DocuSign SOW is required before provisioning reserved keys.

Immediate next steps (please reply inline):
1) Confirm the CIDR/IPs we should allow (example attached: network-allowlist-20261012.txt)
2) Who is our technical contact for VPC peering? (name + email)
3) Preferred start date for brokered peering: week of Oct 19 or Oct 26?

If you want, Marissa from our SE team can triage the peering prep and run a quick network readiness call.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0142

Date: 2026-10-13T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: org + network MAP and POC environment checklist

Great, thanks Raj. Quick answers and what we'll prepare on our side:

1) API keys & org setup
- We'll create a temporary evaluation organization (org ID will be shared when ready) and issue time-limited API keys (default expiry 30 days, can shorten on request). Keys will be scoped to a dedicated evaluation model bundle and will be tagged to your account for telemetry.

2) Logging & retention
- For the POC we retain request/response logs for 14 days by default in the managed console; we can provide a longer retention window if needed (extra add-on). We'll include a log export to your S3 bucket if preferred (needs a short IAM role setup).

3) VPC peering & allowlist
- Marissa will run the peering readiness checklist. For peering we ask for: peer VPC ID, region, one /28 for peering endpoints, and the egress IPs for allowlist. If you prefer managed egress, we can use our NAT with allowed CIDRs.

Proposed schedule (two-week MAP):
- Oct 13–15: finalize CIDRs, security contact, and procurement path
- Oct 18: network prep call (60m) + handoff to Marissa
- Oct 19–23: VPC peering + org provisioning + API keys issued
- Oct 26–30: ingest sample workload and initial perf/eval (latency/cost metrics)

I attached a slightly updated MAP with a task owner column (MAP_DataHealth_v0.3.xlsx). Please confirm: 1) CIDRs, 2) security contact, 3) preferred peering start window (Oct 19 vs Oct 26).

Thanks — looping Diego from infra for any low-level network questions.

Best,
Soojin

Subject: RE: POC: org + network MAP and POC environment checklist

Looping in Diego for peering specifics. Quick tech notes for Raj (internal copy to Soojin):

- Ports: we need outbound 443 (HTTPS) from DataHealth to Redwood endpoints. For peering, the control plane uses TCP 443 plus a healthcheck port we negotiate in the peering call.
- NAT vs direct egress: if you choose direct peering, we'll provision a small peering endpoint in your VPC and route to our ingress subnet. If you prefer simpler ops, allowlisting egress CIDRs to our managed NAT is faster (no routing changes on your side).
- Suggested ephemeral CIDR for management endpoints: 10.250.254.0/28 (we'll hand over the exact /28 once you confirm peering).

I can host the network prep call on Oct 18 at 10:00 AM PT — works for your team? Agenda: verify CIDRs, IAM role for S3 export (if chosen), and peering window.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
